*grace's cases is back with a look at a potential emerging trend in nba brand deals* :eyes: 
_topline: the boys are capitalizing on self-care instead of self-destruction !!!_ 

*partnership one: kevin durant x cerave* 
• 2021: a close up photo of his leg goes viral because it's literally grey, he's dragged to oblivion by fellow players, sports media, the entire internet
• Dec. 2025, <https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/kevin-durant-explains-why-stopped-121500536.html|he goes on his teammates podcast> and talks about not caring about taking care of himself (<https://www.tiktok.com/@allthesmoke/video/7594916220219018551|haircuts, lotion, showering>), ball is the only thing on his mind, gets clowned again  
• Jan 27, he posts a video on Twitter — in addition to being a future hall of fame hooper, he is one of our worlds most prolific twitter users — of him reading mean tweets about his ashy leg. caption: <https://x.com/KDTrey5/status/2016165167067775348|Y’all keep bringing up my legs…might be time to address it with @cerave? #ad> (2M views)
• Feb 10, he drops video 2, announcing him as <https://x.com/KDTrey5/status/2021238091072090574|The New Face of Legs>, 40M views in 48 hours just on Twitter, <https://www.instagram.com/reel/DUlO61RE1Gl/|another 10 on IG>, and tons of spinoff coverage with millions more views 
• The <https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/nba-superstar-kevin-durant-becomes-the-new-face-of-legs-in-ceraves-latest-moisturize-like-a-derm-campaign-302682845.html|brand positioning>: _"CeraVe is teaming up with Durant to destigmatize "skincidents" – those viral, unexpected moments when neglected, dry skin is revealed to the world."_
*partnership two: jaylen brown x nutrafol* 
• 2022: i think it was this season that jaylen brown traded in his flat top and started wearing braids 
• 2024: whatever the hair version of a "skincident" is, jb was at the center of ruthless ridicule online <https://x.com/WhiteBballPains/status/1788630125476491677|over his "at&t logo braids"> where you could see the patches of hair loss or recession (still won the nba championship and finals mvp, the man loves a hater)
• Mar 2025: finally buzzes his hair at the end of ramadan 
• Oct 2025: new nba season starts, jb has some new offerings on and off the court — he's streaming on twitch after games (obsessed) and ... he's leaving his mark on other players, literally. it becomes readily apparent that he's using black hairspray to make his hair look fuller and it <https://x.com/motts_apple/status/1981897825173860707|comes off like a stamp> on OG anunoby's white knicks jersey during the game, millions and millions of views 
    ◦ he starts to take control of the narrative, <https://x.com/OhhMar24/status/1983314497004826739|streaming on twitch with his barber, asking "chat am i cooked,"> hanging with the boys and confronting all the chatter 
    ◦ decides to leave lebron james (who is also a target of hair trolling) a voicemail on stream to ask him "<https://www.tmz.com/2025/10/29/jaylen-brown-lebron-hairline-stain-jersey-video/|Turkey or no Turkey ... and I ain't talking no cheese sandwich.>" 
• Nov 2025: <https://x.com/TheNBACentel/status/1986259611452625266|happens again>, <https://x.com/ESPNNBA/status/1988763191967371510|shaq made fun of him> on espn, <https://x.com/BleacherReport/status/1986804562825814284|rick ross makes a video> telling him to stop, containment is broken — jb starts lobbying beyonce for cecred hair products 
• Dec 2025: he takes full control of the narrative — announcing he's <https://www.instagram.com/p/DSh9LE_iKst/|partnering with nutrafol> to go on the hair journey together and he'll continue to talk about his progress on stream  
    ◦ just to add some jb flair, he says players who he stamped should feel lucky that they have "<https://x.com/LegionHoops/status/2002815065985278360|the residue of a champion>" on them 
i think mental health was the first frontier for male athletes to conquer and some of them have done that well. self-care is absolutely the second. very interesting stuff here!

attachments.text:
I’m a political influencer. Here’s exactly how much the Left and the Right were willing to pay me.

Before the 2024 election, you couldn’t easily gauge my partisanship on my largest platform (~2 million followers), where I interview retired spies and intelligence officials. If you really listened to the themes, you might have guessed I lean Democrat… but most PACs and political advertisers didn’t do that level of homework.

By September 2024, I was getting inbound from funders on both sides of the aisle.

The difference in rate for the exact same deliverable floored me.

Left: $2,000 for one video
Right: $36,000 for one video

Same format. Same audience size. Same production lift.

A 1,700% difference.

Because of my values, I worked with organizations on the left and declined the offers on the right.

But let’s be honest: for many creators, that delta makes the decision for you.
For influencers, brand deals aren’t “extra.” They’re rent. They’re healthcare. They’re payroll for editors. When someone offers you the equivalent of several months’ income for one deliverable, it’s not an abstract ethical debate; it’s survival math.

And if you’re a lifestyle, sports, or comedy creator who doesn’t deeply care about politics? The incentive structure nudges you in one direction.

Now zoom out.

According to the Pew Research Center, roughly 1 in 5 U.S. adults regularly get news from influencers. Among adults under 30, that number jumps to nearly 40%.

Meanwhile, a 2024 analysis from Media Matters for America found that 9 of the 10 most popular online political shows are right-leaning, based on cross-platform following and engagement.

The right didn’t win the digital attention war by accident.
They treated creators like infrastructure.
The economics are simple.

Progressive campaigns will spend tens of thousands of dollars on Meta ad buys that:
- reach colder audiences
- convert at lower rates
- disappear into the scroll

Meanwhile, creators offer:
- built-in trust
- niche credibility
- community-driven amplification
- repeat exposure

Influencer partnerships aren’t just impressions. They’re relational persuasion.

And yet, investment on the left consistently lags, both in rate and in scale.

I’ve seen some movement as we approach the midterms. There’s acknowledgment that this gap exists. But rates remain lower, and budgets remain cautious compared to the right’s ecosystem-wide approach.

Here’s the uncomfortable truth:
If you underpay in a market economy, you shouldn’t be surprised when supply flows elsewhere.

Creators are rational actors responding to incentives.

If one side offers 18x the rate for the same work, it will shape the ideological makeup of the influencer economy over time, not necessarily because creators are ideologues, but because they are business owners.

The political influencer ecosystem isn’t *just* about ideas.

It’s about capital allocation.

And right now, capital is not evenly distributed. | 48 comments on LinkedIn

There’s been a pretty big update on LinkedIn formats. PDF carousels are now showing up smaller in-feed on desktop, which means they’re taking up less screen space and receiving less engagement.

I thinkkk LinkedIn has realised everyone clocked that carousels were becoming an engagement hack. Interestingly though, carousel ads are still staying the same larger size. Just been studying what's working in feeds. This just happened this week so still learning!

 *Desktop view:* The best posts on LinkedIn organically seems to be photo posts using no more than four images, making sure the first visual is really clear and easy to process. On desktop, these take up significantly more feed real estate than PDF carousels now.

*Mobile view:* Everything is effectively the same smaller carousel format anyway. PDFs, photos, carousels all end up looking relatively similar in size there.
I still think a huge amount of LinkedIn usage happens on a desktop, during the workday, especially Monday to Thursday when we typically see the biggest spikes in activity. But people absolutely still use LinkedIn on weekends, on commutes, and during downtime on mobile too.

Something to think about for our internal comms!

May Update: Instagram keeps doubling down on carousels :rotating_light: 

The latest test?

Adding a different caption to each slide within a carousel.

And honestly, this could be a bigger shift than it sounds :point_up::skin-tone-3:

Carousels were already outperforming for many creators because they:
→ Increase time spent on post 
→ Encourage swipes and saves 
→ Give Instagram more engagement signals to work with 

Now imagine each slide becoming its own mini-story. 

This opens the door for:
 :jigsaw: Step-by-step storytelling
 :mortar_board: Deeper educational content
 :fishing_pole_and_fish: Slide-by-slide hooks
 :art: More context without overcrowding visuals
 :arrows_counterclockwise: Stronger retention across the carousel

Now the big question: when will this actually be available for everyone? 

For now, Instagram says it’s only being tested with a limited group of users, and there’s no official rollout timeline yet.

But considering how aggressively Instagram has been evolving carousel functionality lately, this feels less like an experiment and more like a preview of where the platform is heading.

PS: No, I’m not one of the lucky testers of this new feature. Are you? Please tell us everything :eyes:
